explanations: terra: Buying error for guidance makes ضَلال a failed exchange of direction; it develops the source's opposition without a literal travel scene.
luna: This verse describes people as dead, then given life, then dying and being revived before returning to God; it makes earthly disappearance one stage in a movement to a destination.
terra: After descent to earth, following God's guidance removes fear and grief, framing earthly life as a passage whose direction determines its outcome.

luna: The verse uses the image of the calf being made to enter the hearts of the Israelites; as a metaphor, it parallels the section’s swallowed thing disappearing from sight while reaching an inward destination.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل is used with the way itself: whoever exchanges belief for disbelief has strayed from سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ, a direct instance of losing the route. | terra: Changing faith for disbelief makes a person ضَلَّ from the even way; this names the departure from a route whose straightness the source contrasts with loss.

luna: A traveler sees a ruined town and asks how God will give it life after death; God makes him die for a hundred years and revives him, turning apparent disappearance into a demonstrated return. | terra: The man who passes a ruined town is made dead for a hundred years and then raised; his question about life after ruin makes vanished life a divinely reversible interval.
terra: Abraham's scattered bird-parts are called and come swiftly, a concrete scene in which what has been dispersed beyond ordinary sight returns to a summons.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل has a dictionary branch for an event disappearing from memory; here أَنْ تَضِلَّ إِحْدَاهُمَا is paired with the other woman reminding her, showing how a lost recollection is recovered. | terra: تَضِلَّ describes one witness's memory failing so the other can remind her, the source's explicit secondary sense of ضَلَل as something lost from remembrance.
terra: Jesus commands worship of God and calls it a straight path; this repeated formulation gives the source's road a worshipful direction.
terra: Holding fast to God is described as being guided to a straight path, giving the source's route a relation of attachment rather than mere movement.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل appears in the wish that others lose the way; this verse says some People of the Book want believers to تَضِلُّوا السَّبِيلَ, making misdirection an intended diversion from a route.
terra: For one whom God leaves astray, no path can be found; the verse joins the source's loss-word to the failure to locate a route.

terra: An emigrant who leaves home toward God and His Messenger may be overtaken by death on the road, yet his reward is already due from God; the path's destination survives incomplete visible travel.
terra: Those who hold fast to God enter mercy and are guided to Him on a straight path; the wording makes the endpoint of صِرَاط explicit.
terra: Breaking the covenant after its pledges is described as straying from the even way, an explicit moral departure from a route.

luna: The section’s named root ص ر ط depicts a route that takes a traveler somewhere; here guidance leads from darkness to light and to the straight path, specifying the change and destination of the journey. | terra: Through revelation God leads to paths of peace, brings people from darkness to light, and guides to a straight path; visibility and destination reinforce the source's image.

luna: The section links ض ل ل to the traveler’s course; this verse describes people who strayed from the sound way and led many others astray, turning the path image into a chain of diverted travelers. | terra: People who went astray, led many astray, and strayed from the level way show ضَلَال as social misdirection that leaves the proper route.

luna: The section places the disappearance of false partners at the gathering; this verse stages that gathering and asks the associators where their claimed partners are. | terra: The gathering of all the associators supplies the judgment scene in which their claimed partners will prove absent in 6:24; none can disappear from that assembly.

luna: This verse gives the associators’ denial in the gathering scene begun in 6:22; 6:24 then says their fabricated claims have vanished, so this row contributes the denial immediately before that exposure.

luna: The section says fabricated partners disappear from their worshippers at the gathering; this verse states وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ, making the vanished claim itself the focus. | terra: Their inventions ضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ, vanish away from them at judgment, giving the source's loss-image a concrete eschatological scene.

luna: This verse describes deaf and mute people in darkness, then contrasts those God leaves astray with those He places on a straight path; the lost and guided courses are explicit. | terra: Those who deny the signs are deaf and mute in darkness, while God may place another on a straight path; obscured perception and the road are explicitly paired.

luna: The verse says no leaf falls without God knowing it and mentions a grain in earth’s darknesses kept in a clear record; it reverses the section’s image of something hidden as something lost. | terra: Leaves, grain in earth's darkness, and every moist or dry thing remain in a clear record; what is hidden in earth is never lost to the knower who does not يَضِلُّ or forget.
terra: God takes people in sleep at night and raises them by day until an appointed term, then they return to Him; disappearance from waking sight is ordered toward return.

luna: The section distinguishes a traveler who vanishes from view while following a route from someone lost without knowing where he is going; this verse pictures a حَيْرَان person in the land while companions call him toward guidance. | terra: The simile is a person bewildered on the earth after devils have lured him away, while companions call him back to guidance; it is the source's destinationless going versus a called route.
terra: Abraham watches a star set and rejects what disappears; the visible vanishing of a supposed lord begins a scene whose next ayah joins guidance and ضَلَال.

luna: When Abraham sees the star set, he fears being among الضَّالِّين unless his Lord guides him; the disappearing object becomes a concrete occasion for the section’s question of losing direction. | terra: When the moon sets, Abraham says that without his Lord's guidance he would be among the ضَالِّين; disappearing celestial signs and being lost are deliberately adjacent.
terra: The larger sun also disappears, so its setting cannot be the arrival point for Abraham's search; the passage continues the source's contrast between a vanishing object and a true destination.
terra: After the setting lights, Abraham turns his face to the Creator of heavens and earth, giving the preceding failed sightings a directed end.

luna: The section describes what people falsely claim disappearing from them; this verse says they arrive alone, cannot see their claimed intercessors, and وَضَلَّ عَنْكُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ. | terra: Arriving before God one by one, they find the intercessors they claimed gone from them; the verse makes false attachments disappear while persons still arrive.

luna: Stars are made for people to find their way through the darknesses of land and sea, a direct navigation scene where the path is not fully visible but has a destination. | terra: Stars are made so people can find their way through darknesses of land and sea, furnishing visible guidance where the source imagines a traveler gone from sight.
terra: The Lord knows best who strays from His way and who is guided, placing even moral loss within the complete knowledge opposed to losing and forgetting.

luna: The section understands ص ر ط as a course that carries someone onward; this verse calls it the Lord’s straight path, with the following verse naming the abode of peace for those who reach it. | terra: "This is the path of your Lord, straight" assigns the road its owner, a useful counterpart to the source's account of a path that carries someone somewhere.
luna: This verse names the Abode of Peace as the destination of the straight path in 6:126; its own contribution is showing where that directed travel arrives.

luna: The section’s named root ص ر ط presents a route with a direction; this verse says to follow the straight path and not other paths that split people from God’s way, making divergence itself the danger. | terra: God's one straight path is to be followed, while other ways scatter people from it; the source's contrast between directed going and lost dispersal is stated spatially.
terra: The Prophet is guided to a straight path described as an upright religion, showing the source's physical image becoming a communal way of life.

luna: The section’s image is a path along which a traveler advances; Satan says he will sit in wait upon the straight path, placing an adversary directly on that route. | terra: Iblis vows to sit for people on God's straight صِرَاط, making the source's road a contested course with an ambush that can turn travelers away.
terra: Human life, death in the earth, and being brought out of it form a complete movement rather than the final disappearance imagined in the source's quoted objection.

terra: One group is guided while another deserves error because it takes devils as allies yet thinks itself guided; it sharpens the source's contrast between purposeful travel and confident misdirection.
luna: At judgment people ask where their claimed partners are and are told those partners have left them; it is another direct scene of an object disappearing from those who relied on it.

luna: At the judgment gathering, this verse says people who had forgotten the meeting discover the truth and that their fabricated intercessors have vanished; it repeats the section’s disappearance of claims from their makers. | terra: When the promised outcome comes, what they invented has vanished from them; the source's contrast between a real destination and loss is enacted at the Day.
terra: The people are forbidden to sit on every path threatening travelers and seeking crookedness in God's way; the ayah concretely opposes passage and deliberate derailing.
terra: Moses' staff swallows what the magicians had falsified; the source's swallowed-and-gone image meets a scene in which fabrication physically disappears.
terra: Those who see the way of right guidance do not take it, but take the way of error when they see it; the verse reverses the traveler's choice at the fork.
terra: Whomever God guides is guided, while those He leaves astray are the losers; it gives the source's two opposed goings a compressed judgment form.
luna: People with hearts, eyes, and ears who do not perceive are called more astray than cattle; this gives a specific image of having faculties yet failing to find the way.

luna: The section presents the straight path as a route with an arrival; this verse joins the two details by saying God calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path. | terra: God calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, giving the source's path an explicit destination.

luna: This verse stages the gathering of worshippers with the partners they claimed; 10:29 gives the partners’ testimony and 10:30 says the fabrications vanish, so this row contributes the gathering itself. | terra: The Day separates worshippers from their alleged partners, preparing the disappearance of fabricated claims in 10:30 rather than leaving an undifferentiated crowd.
luna: The claimed partners testify that the worshippers were not worshipping them; this supplies the denial within the gathering scene before 10:30 states that the fabrications vanished.

luna: The section describes invented objects disappearing from their makers at judgment; this verse says وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ when every soul faces what it did. | terra: Each soul is tested by what it sent ahead, then its inventions ضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ; claims vanish, but the soul returns to its true Lord.
terra: Not even an atom in earth or heaven is absent from the Lord, and all is in a clear record; this supplies a close Qur'anic counterpart to the source's lost-in-earth claim.

luna: The section uses disappearance in water as an image of loss; after Pharaoh drowns, this verse says his body is saved as a sign for those who come later, a specific reversal of vanishing without trace.

luna: This verse says the wrongdoers lost themselves and their fabrications disappeared from them; it makes both kinds of loss in the section visible at once, the person and what the person invented. | terra: Those people have lost themselves, and what they used to invent disappears from them; loss here consumes both the traveler and the false route imagined for him.
terra: "My Lord is on a straight path" places divine governance itself under the image of a reliable course, not a vanishing or arbitrary one.

luna: The section names غَيَابَتِ الْجُبِّ, the well’s hidden recess: the brothers propose putting Yusuf there so a caravan may take him, a concrete disappearance that is meant to lead somewhere. | terra: The brothers propose the غَيَابَةِ الْجُبِّ, the unseen bottom of a well; the source explicitly reads this disappearance as one that will still carry Joseph onward.

luna: After Yusuf is put in the well, this verse says God reveals that he will later tell his brothers what they did while they remain unaware; the hidden traveler already has a destination beyond the brothers’ sight. | terra: Joseph is actually put into the well's hidden depth, but the divine message there gives that obscurity a future report and therefore an end.

luna: The section describes Yusuf’s concealment in a well as a disappearance that leads to a destination; this verse shows the caravan’s water drawer finding him, so being out of sight has carried him into another people’s hands. | terra: The passing caravan's water-drawer finds Joseph in the well, completing the source's point that this hidden place delivers him into travelers' hands.

luna: The cupbearer forgets to mention Joseph to the king; this is a concrete event lost from memory, one of the section’s stated secondary senses of ض ل ل. | terra: A forgotten mention delays Joseph in prison, a further episode in which memory-loss keeps the already hidden traveler out of sight; the grammatical referent of the forgetting is debated.
terra: The released man remembers Joseph after a time and sets out to ask him, reversing the forgetfulness that prolonged Joseph's obscurity.
terra: Jacob's eyes turn white from grief over Joseph's absence, joining a lost son to the source's concern with vision and an unseen traveler.
terra: When Joseph's shirt reaches Jacob, his sight returns, reversing the blindness born from the earlier disappearance.

luna: The section treats the path as a directed passage with an arrival; this verse describes revelation bringing people from darkness into light and to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy. | terra: The Book brings people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission to the path of the Mighty, a movement from non-seeing toward a marked route.
terra: They turn others from God's way and seek crookedness in it, preferring the nearer life; this is the source's path deprived of its proper end.
terra: The messengers say God has guided them in their ways; their trust amid harm gives plural routes a destination anchored in Him.
terra: God calls the protected line of access a straight صِرَاط upon Him, locating the route's security in a divine guarantee.
terra: God takes responsibility for the direction of the way, while another way is crooked; this is the source's distinction between a route with an end and a going that misses it.

luna: This verse describes rivers and roads through the land as means of guidance; it gives a concrete landscape version of the section’s path that carries travelers toward an intended direction. | terra: Mountains, rivers, and ways are placed in the earth so people may be guided, showing the ground as terrain supplied with orientation rather than a place of mere loss.

luna: The signs and stars here guide travelers; this specifies how a route can still lead somewhere when the traveler relies on markers rather than direct sight of the destination. | terra: Landmarks and stars guide travelers, a concrete answer to the source's concern with the person whose whereabouts and direction are unknown.

luna: This verse describes pure milk emerging from between waste and blood; unlike the section’s dictionary example of milk disappearing into water, the milk keeps a distinct identity through a hidden passage.
terra: The man who enjoins justice is himself on a straight path; the source's road-image is applied to a person's upright agency rather than physical travel.
terra: Seeing the partners they had associated exposes the alleged guides before 16:87 says their inventions have vanished; the visual encounter makes the later loss specific.

luna: The section describes false claims disappearing from their worshippers on the final day; this verse says their inventions are lost from them when they submit to God. | terra: On that Day they yield to God and their inventions vanish from them, another explicit judgment form of the source's ضَلَّ-as-gone-away.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل is paired here with inability to find a way: the opponents have strayed and cannot find سَبِيلًا, matching loss as movement without a known destination. | terra: Their hostile descriptions leave them ضَلُّوا so they cannot find a way, an explicit form of the source's unlocated and directionless going.
luna: The section quotes the objection that people lost in earth cannot be recreated; this verse repeats the objection in terms of bones and fragments becoming a new creation.
luna: In answer to the objection in 17:49, this verse says even stone or iron would not exceed God’s power to restore; it treats changed material as no escape from return.
luna: This verse asks who will restore even a seemingly greater creation and answers, the One who created them the first time; it makes bodily change no barrier to return.
luna: After the restoration exchange in 17:51, this verse says God will call people and they will respond with praise; it names the meeting that follows the apparent disappearance in death.
terra: In danger at sea, all whom they call upon disappear from them except God; water makes the source's image of something lost in water into a test of the only reliable destination.
terra: After the sea emergency of 17:67, the warning shifts to land that may swallow people; neither water nor ground provides a place to vanish beyond divine reach.

luna: The section links losing the path with not knowing where one goes; this verse joins blindness in this life with greater ضَلَالًا عَنِ السَّبِيلِ in the next, extending the lost route beyond death. | terra: One blind in this life is blind in the next and further astray in way; physical non-seeing is made a path condition.
terra: The cave scene says that one whom God sends astray will not find a guiding protector, so the physically sheltered travelers are framed by the problem of finding direction.
luna: The command to remember God when one forgets gives a direct memory-loss instance, matching the section’s dictionary sense of an event disappearing from recollection.
terra: A garden's water may sink into the ground so that its owner cannot pursue it, a concrete counterpart to something becoming inaccessible in earth.
terra: The guilty see the Fire, know they will fall into it, and find no escape; unlike the imagined disappearance, judgment fixes an unavoidable arrival.

luna: The section’s dictionary examples include a thing lost in water and something gone from memory; this verse joins both in the fish forgotten by Moses and his companion as it takes its way into the sea. | terra: At the meeting of the seas, the fish takes its way into the sea; a thing becoming invisible in water is described through a way, echoing the source's water-loss and route imagery.

luna: The companion later says نسِيتُ الْحُوتَ and recounts that the fish took its way in the sea; his explanation makes the water-disappearance and lost memory in 18:61 explicit. | terra: The servant says he forgot the fish just as it took its way into the sea, combining the source's memory-loss sense with disappearance in water.
terra: The lost fish-sign becomes the route they were seeking, and they return by tracing their steps; disappearance here guides travelers to their intended meeting.

luna: The section’s examples make disappearance different from erasure; the treasure hidden beneath the wall is preserved for two orphans until the right time, so concealment can protect what is meant to arrive.
terra: Mary wishes she had become a thing forgotten, a specific image of disappearing from human memory that expands the source's memory sense of loss.
terra: Jesus' call to worship God concludes, "this is a straight path," repeating the path as a spoken summons rather than an abstract word.
terra: Abraham asks his father to follow him so he can guide him to an even path; guidance is offered as a personal redirection away from a perilous attachment.
terra: "Your Lord is not forgetful" repeats the boundary stated in 20:52: what humans forget does not vanish from divine care.

luna: The section pairs its named root ض ل ل with forgetting; Musa answers Firʿawn’s question about past generations in 20:51 by saying his Lord neither يَضِلُّ nor يَنسَى, so the vanished past is not lost to divine knowledge. | terra: Moses says of the record of past generations that his Lord neither loses track, لَا يَضِلُّ, nor forgets; it directly reverses both source senses of ضَلَل as loss and failed memory.

luna: The verse says God made roads through the earth so people can travel; this is a physical counterpart to the section’s road as a directed passage. | terra: Immediately after the Lord who does not lose or forget, He makes paths through the earth; known-making and route-making meet in the same reply.
terra: From earth God creates people, returns them to it, and brings them out again; burial has both a source and a specified exit.
terra: Moses' staff will swallow what the magicians made, another clear instance of fabricated work being made to disappear through swallowing.
terra: Moses is told to make a dry path through the sea for the servants, a literal route across water that protects travelers from being overtaken.
terra: Pharaoh follows them with his forces and the sea overwhelms him; the same water marks the boundary between a guided route and engulfing loss.
terra: The verse names Pharaoh as one who led his people astray and did not guide them, interpreting the sea scene in the source's terms of destinationless leadership.
terra: Adam forgot, giving a human instance of memory's lapse beside the source's dictionary explanation of ضَلال as loss from remembrance.
terra: Whoever follows divine guidance will neither go astray nor suffer; this directly pairs a route with escape from the destinationless ضَلَال of the source.
terra: Turning from the reminder yields a constricted life and resurrection blind, extending the source's blind would-be traveler beyond 36:66.
terra: The resurrected person asks why he is raised blind although he once saw, making lost sight a judgment condition rather than just a physical obstacle.
terra: Because he forgot God's signs, he is forgotten that Day; memory loss receives the reciprocal boundary that contrasts with 20:52's unfailing divine memory.
terra: The closing challenge says people will know who are companions of the even path and who is guided, postponing the visible distinction until a decisive arrival.
terra: God makes broad passes and paths in the earth so people may be guided; the terrain itself is arranged for a route.
terra: Whoever takes Satan as patron is led astray and then led toward the punishment of the blaze, a false guide whose course has a ruinous destination.

luna: This verse describes people created from dust and a dead earth revived into growth; it makes burial and the earth’s apparent lifelessness a passage toward renewed life. | terra: Human formation from dust, death, and the reviving of dead earth culminate in the raising of those in graves; the buried body is not an untraceable disappearance.

luna: The verse says the Hour is coming and God will raise those in the graves; it directly gives a destination beyond the section’s image of the dead disappearing into earth. | terra: The certain Hour includes God's raising all who are in graves, stating the final result toward which 22:5's body-and-earth signs point.
terra: Travel through the earth should awaken hearts, yet the verse says it is hearts that become blind; it deepens the source's blind traveler beyond eyesight.
terra: Believers recognize the revealed truth and are guided by God to a straight path, presenting reception of truth as entry onto the route.
terra: After earthly life people die, naming the entrance into the hidden state that the next ayah will reverse.
terra: After death in 23:15, people are raised on the Day of Resurrection, giving that disappearance a specified future end.

luna: The section’s named root ص ر ط is used here for the straight path to which the Messenger calls people; the verse makes the route an offered direction rather than an aimless disappearance. | terra: The Prophet calls people to a straight path; the direct address carries the same guiding stance as Surah 1's request for guidance.
luna: The section contrasts a path that reaches somewhere with being lost; this verse says those who reject the Hereafter turn aside from الصراط, naming the route’s contrary direction.
luna: The section describes those who think burial is an end; this verse repeats their question whether they will be raised after dying and becoming dust and bones.
luna: This verse gives the objectors’ conclusion that resurrection is an old fable; its own contribution is the denial that the section’s disappearance-under-earth image has a later destination.

luna: The section contrasts a road that reaches its destination with loss that leaves no arrival; the disbelievers’ deeds are a mirage that seems to promise water, but when the seeker reaches it he finds nothing. | terra: A thirsty traveler takes a mirage for water, reaches it, and finds nothing but finds God; a false apparent destination exposes the difference between seeming and true arrival.
terra: Deep-sea darkness makes a person scarcely see his own hand; this nonlexical water scene intensifies the source's inability to see a way, though it does not name a road.
terra: God guides whom He wills to a straight path after making signs clear; it connects a visible sign with the capacity to take a route.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل describes a traveler with no known way; at the gathering, God asks whether the worshipped beings led people astray or whether the people themselves ضَلُّوا السَّبِيلَ. | terra: At the gathering, the beings once worshipped are asked whether they led the servants astray or the servants themselves lost the way; false companions and lost direction meet in one judgment scene.

luna: The worshipped beings answer the question in 25:17 by saying their followers forgot the reminder and became a people بُورًا; the response continues the scene of followers left without the destination they imagined.
terra: A companion leads someone astray from the Reminder after it reaches him, a social counterpart to the source's traveler diverted from a destination.
terra: Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are worst in place and furthest astray in way, giving the source's road a reversed bodily orientation and end.
terra: Moses calls his earlier act one done while among the ضَالِّين; the different sense of the source word marks error before later direction, though no road is pictured.
terra: Moses' staff swallows what the magicians fabricated, repeating the physical disappearance of false making that anticipates false claims vanishing at judgment.
terra: Moses strikes the sea and it parts, making a traversable passage through water where the source contrasts a directing path with engulfing loss.
terra: God saves Moses and all who are with him through the opened sea, stating the successful arrival of the route begun in 26:63.
terra: The remaining pursuers are drowned, so the same water marks the contrary end to the protected passage.
terra: Solomon notices the hoopoe absent from sight, an instance of غَائِبين that becomes a purposeful journey when the bird returns; the link is lexical and scenic rather than about ضَلال.
terra: The hoopoe returns after only a short absence with news from Saba, making an apparent disappearance a directed mission rather than loss.
luna: The section’s root ض ل ل describes loss of direction; this verse says Satan turned the people away from the way while they thought themselves guided, a specific case of hidden misdirection.
terra: God guides through darknesses of land and sea, bringing the source's lost traveler into the very environments where orientation can fail.

luna: This verse says the Messenger cannot guide blind people out of their error; it parallels the section’s blind people rushing toward a path they cannot see. | terra: The Messenger cannot guide the blind away from their error, closely echoing the source's image of people at the road who cannot see.

luna: The section says a traveler can disappear from sight while still reaching a destination; Moses’ mother is told to cast him in the river with the promise إِنَّا رَادُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ, making the water journey purposeful.
luna: This verse continues Moses’ river journey by showing Pharaoh’s household picking him up; it contributes the arrival after the child has been hidden from his mother’s sight.
luna: This verse completes the river journey by returning Moses to his mother so her eyes may be comforted; the one lost from sight is shown to have reached the promised destination.
terra: Leaving toward Midian, Moses asks that his Lord guide him to the sound way; a traveler actually seeks orientation and a destination.
terra: Following desire without guidance from God is called the greatest ضَلال, specifying an inner impulse that produces the source's directionless going.
luna: At the gathering, this verse says the proof is shown and what people invented has vanished from them; it gives the section’s lost claim a courtroom setting.

terra: Korah and his dwelling are swallowed by the earth, a severe physical counterimage to burial's promised emergence; it illuminates ground's power to remove someone from view, though not the source's ضَلال wording.
luna: This verse asks people to consider how God begins creation and repeats it; it treats apparent ending as a passage that can be followed by a new beginning.
terra: "Travel through the earth" to see first creation is followed by God's bringing forth the later creation, coupling an earthly journey with resurrection from what seems past.
luna: The people who made idols objects of affection in this life disavow and curse one another at Resurrection; it shows the claimed bond disappearing at the final meeting.
terra: Those who strive are guided in God's ways; plural ways retain the source's sense of purposeful movement toward God.

luna: This verse says God brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and revives earth after its death; disappearance is one stage in a repeated passage. | terra: God brings living from dead, revives the earth after its death, and says people will likewise be brought out; earth's apparent finality is a sign of emergence.
luna: This verse states that God begins creation and then repeats it; its own contribution is to make return after disappearance part of the same creative course.

luna: The verse directs attention to traces of mercy and asks how God gives life to earth after its death; it reverses the image of earth as the final place where life disappears. | terra: The reviving effects of God's mercy on dead earth are explicitly offered as evidence that He gives life to the dead.

luna: This repeats the blind person’s inability to be guided out of error, but adds that only those who believe the signs can be made to hear; it develops the section’s contrast between sightless movement and guidance. | terra: Again, blind people cannot be guided away from their error; the wording preserves the relation between blindness and not leaving ضَلَال.

luna: This verse describes speech purchased to lead people astray from God’s way; it gives a concrete means by which a traveler can be diverted from the section’s guided road. | terra: One buys distracting talk to lead people astray from God's way without knowledge, contrasting a made-lost route with the source's directed صِرَاط.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل (ḍ-l-l) appears in ضَلَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ: the speakers treat being lost in earth as an end, while the verse makes that disappearance the question of renewed creation. | terra: The source's "lost in the earth" is the challengers' ضَلَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ: burial is treated as erasure, while the ayah exposes their denial of meeting their Lord.
terra: The reply to 32:10 gives the supposedly vanished person a fixed course: the angel takes them at death and then they are returned to their Lord.

luna: The section describes dalal as a person with no known destination; people here confess that their leaders أَضَلُّونَا السَّبِيلَا, identifying other people as the cause of their lost route. | terra: In the Fire, followers say their leaders led them astray; the verse supplies a social form of the source's traveler whose direction was seized by another.
terra: Nothing of an atom's weight in heaven or earth escapes God's knowledge, however small; physical disappearance never makes a creature unaccountable.
luna: The deniers ask whether they will be created anew after being torn apart; this repeats the section’s question about whether bodily disappearance into fragments is final.
terra: The warning that God can cause the earth to swallow people gives a living, catastrophic counterimage to burial in earth and shows that ground is never beyond His control.
terra: Visible towns and measured stages are set between places of travel, so a journey has recognizable stops and safe arrival rather than unknown whereabouts.
terra: After asking for longer stages between their journeys, the people are scattered; their disrupted travel contrasts with the measured route of 34:18.
terra: The Messenger says that if he strays it is against himself, while guidance comes by revelation; the first-person contrast separates lost motion from a received direction.
terra: A person's evil action is made fair to him while God guides or lets astray; mistaken sight of one's own course parallels the false confidence of those who think themselves guided.

luna: Winds drive clouds to dead land, and God gives life to the earth after its death; the scene makes lifeless ground a passage to renewed life, paralleling the burial image. | terra: God revives dead land by wind and cloud and says such is the resurrection; earth's apparent lifelessness becomes a sign that buried life is not simply gone.
terra: The Messenger is declared to be upon a straight path, supplying the guiding speaker who stands opposite the blind runners of 36:66.

luna: The section says the dead’s disappearance into earth is not the end but a way to meeting; this verse has people hurry out of their graves toward their Lord when the trumpet is blown. | terra: At the Trumpet people hurry out from graves toward their Lord; the journey from buried disappearance has a named recipient.

luna: After the emergence in 36:51, this verse identifies the graves as a seeming sleep and the awakening as the promise of the Most Merciful; its own contribution is naming the destination reached after concealment. | terra: Those emerging from graves ask who raised them from their resting place, directly continuing 36:51's visible rush toward the Lord.
terra: A single blast brings them all before God, completing the gathering that prevents any buried person from remaining lost.

luna: The section’s named root ص ر ط appears in this chapter as the straight path of worship; this verse identifies the path whose visibility and traversal become the issue in 36:66. | terra: "Worship Me; this is a straight path" gives the route a concrete act of allegiance in the same passage that later pictures blindness at the path.
terra: Satan has led a great multitude astray, supplying the immediate misguiding force that makes 36:66's blind rush toward the path intelligible.

luna: The section’s named root ص ر ط presents a road along which a traveler passes from sight; here people rush along الصراط after their eyes are obscured, separating movement on a way from the ability to see it. | terra: If their eyes were obliterated, they would race for the صِّرَاط but be unable to see: the section's blind traveler and road are staged together.

luna: Following the blinded rush on the path in 36:66, this verse says that if God willed they could neither move forward nor return; it supplies a boundary between a traversable route and complete loss of movement.

luna: This verse presents the resurrection objection through decayed bones and a question about who can revive them, a direct counterpart to the section’s dead hidden in earth. | terra: The skeptic points to decayed bones and asks who can revive them; this is the bodily version of the source's question about being lost in earth.

luna: The answer says the one who created them the first time will revive them; the apparent loss of bodily form is not the end of their path. | terra: The answer is that the original Creator gives the bones life and knows every creation, answering disappearance with complete knowledge and recreation.
luna: The section’s buried dead are hidden from sight; this verse asks whether they will be raised after becoming dust and bones, repeating that disappearance as an objection.
luna: This verse extends the objection in 37:16 to earlier generations, making the disappearance across generations part of the same question.
luna: The answer to the dust-and-bones question is yes, and they will be humbled; this verse supplies the destination that the objectors deny.

luna: The section’s straight road carries a traveler toward an end; this verse commands that the wrongdoers be guided to صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ, an explicitly contrary destination. | terra: The angels are told to lead people to the path of Hell; a named صِرَاط can therefore be an opposite destination to the path requested in Surah 1.
luna: This verse says people found their fathers astray; it makes the section’s lost direction a condition inherited from those who went before.
luna: The next verse says they hasten along their fathers’ footsteps; its contribution is movement along a route inherited from those described as lost in 37:69.
terra: Moses and Aaron's people are guided to a straight path, a historical community-level realization of the route requested in Surah 1.

luna: The section explains ص ر ط through the dictionary image of food swallowed and passing out of sight; Jonah is swallowed by the fish, a human disappearing inside a body while the following verses distinguish that from being lost forever. | terra: The fish swallows Jonah, making him disappear into an unseen interior; like the source's swallowed morsel, loss from sight does not settle his ultimate destination.

luna: After the fish swallows Jonah in 37:142, this verse says his being among the glorifiers is the condition that prevents permanent confinement; it supplies the route’s limit rather than leaving the disappearance final. | terra: Had Jonah not glorified God, he would have remained in the fish until the resurrection; the hidden enclosure is explicitly bounded by an end.
luna: This verse completes the fish scene by setting the alternative duration, remaining in its belly until the day people are raised; the swallowed person’s disappearance has a boundary and release.
terra: God casts Jonah onto an open shore, completing the movement from swallowed invisibility to visible arrival.

luna: David is told not to follow desire lest it lead him astray from God’s way; the verse specifies how a person can leave a route with a known destination. | terra: Following desire leads a judge away from God's path, making inner desire a force that diverts a traveler from a known direction.

luna: God takes souls at death and sleep, retaining those whose death He decrees and returning the others until an appointed term; unseen absence is shown as custody with a defined endpoint. | terra: God takes souls at death and during sleep, retaining some and sending others back; disappearance from waking sight has an ordered custody and return.
luna: This verse introduces the judgment question of where the claimed partners are; 40:74 gives the answer that they have departed, so this row contributes the search for what has vanished.

luna: The section says false partners disappear from those who relied on them; when asked where they are, people here answer that they have departed from them and admit they had called on nothing. | terra: Asked where their partners are, they answer, "ضَلُّوا عَنَّا"; the imagined companions have vanished at the moment of arrival before God.
luna: Thamud are shown the way but prefer blindness to guidance; this is a specific reversal of the section’s traveler who can pass from sight yet remain on a directed course.
terra: Barren earth stirs and grows when water descends; the verse expressly makes its revivification a sign that God gives life to the dead.

luna: This verse says what people invoked before has vanished from them and they have no escape; it directly parallels the section’s lost false objects and the boundary of judgment. | terra: Those formerly invoked vanish from the people, who then know they have no escape; disappearance here is a boundary, not a way out of judgment.
terra: God chooses and guides toward Himself those who turn back, making the terminus of guidance personal and divine rather than merely directional.

luna: Those God leaves astray have no protector, and when they see punishment they ask whether there is a way back; this directly depicts losing both direction and a return route. | terra: Whoever God lets go astray has no protector after Him, setting a boundary on the source's hope that an unlocated traveler can find another guide.
terra: Revelation is made a light by which the Messenger guides servants to a straight path, joining the source's road to the ability to see it.
terra: That path is God's, and all matters finally return to Him; the neighbor makes the path's final arrival explicit.

luna: This verse says God made roads in the earth so people may be guided; it links the road itself with the arrival of guidance, as the section’s straight-path image does. | terra: The earth is made a cradle and paths are made in it so people may be guided, directly joining ground, route, and intended guidance.

luna: The section distinguishes a way that reaches its end from a person led off course; here one who turns away from the reminder is paired with a satanic companion, setting up the diversion described in 43:37. | terra: Whoever turns from the Reminder receives a devil as companion, a false fellow-traveler who will be shown in the next ayah to turn people from the path.

luna: This verse says the companions turn people away from السَّبِيل while they think they are guided, a precise case of losing the route without knowing it. | terra: Those companions bar people from the path while they think themselves guided, the precise danger of moving confidently without a true destination.
terra: The question asks whether the Messenger can guide the blind and one in manifest error, giving the source's blind-on-the-road scene a prophetic address.
terra: Jesus again commands worship of God and identifies it as a straight path, a repeated speaker-and-route formulation alongside 3:51 and 19:36.
terra: A person who takes desire as god is left astray despite knowledge and sealed in hearing and sight; inner misdirection is linked to a failure of perception.
luna: The deniers say only worldly life exists and that time destroys them; this states explicitly the view that disappearance in death has no destination.
luna: The next verse says their only argument when revelation is recited is to demand their forefathers be brought back; it continues their denial that the dead have a destination.

luna: The verse asks who is further astray than those who call on beings that cannot answer until Resurrection and are unaware of the calls; it depicts reliance on an absent destination. | terra: Those who call beings unable to answer until resurrection are called most astray; absent addressees anticipate the source's scenes of vanished false companions.
luna: When people are gathered, the invoked beings become enemies and deny the worship; this completes the nonresponse in 46:5 and the section’s image of vanished claims.
terra: The believing jinn say the Book guides to truth and to a straight way, treating revelation as a reliable direction rather than an unmarked departure.
terra: One who refuses the caller to God cannot escape in the earth and has no protectors; ignoring a summons is called clear error rather than a way out.
terra: God makes the deeds of those who reject and bar His path go lost, extending ضَلال to a life's work that fails to arrive.
terra: For disbelievers, God makes their deeds go lost; this is a secondary disappearance of what they had sent ahead.
luna: The promised rivers include milk whose taste does not change; this contrasts the section’s dictionary image of milk losing its identity in water with milk that remains distinct.
terra: Forgiveness, completion of favor, and guidance to a straight path make the source's road a mercifully sustained course.

luna: The section quotes the denial that people who disappear into earth can be recreated; this verse repeats the question about death and becoming dust, presenting burial as apparent disappearance before 50:4 answers it.

luna: The section’s dictionary sense of ض ل ل includes the dead buried and hidden; this verse says what the earth diminishes of people remains in a preserving record, so hidden from sight does not mean lost to God. | terra: "We know what the earth diminishes of them" and a preserved record answer the fear in 32:10: the earth's taking of bodies is measured, not an untraceable loss.
terra: Rain gives life to dead land, and the ayah says that such is the coming forth; what lies inert in earth is linked to resurrection.
terra: The earth splits open and people hurry out; the gathering is declared easy for God, reversing the image of bodies swallowed beyond recovery.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل pictures loss of direction; this verse negates that loss for the Prophet, so the route carrying revelation is distinguished from aimless wandering. | terra: The Messenger has neither gone astray nor erred; the denial uses ضَلال in its path sense and sets a boundary around prophetic direction.
terra: People follow conjecture and desire although guidance has come; the contrast makes a route available yet refused.
terra: God knows best who has strayed from His path and who is guided, returning the source's unknown whereabouts to complete divine knowledge.
terra: The final end is with the Lord; it supplies the destination denied by the idea that burial makes a person simply vanish.
terra: They emerge from graves and rush toward the caller, a crowd no longer unlocated but summoned along a determined course.
terra: The guilty are in error and a blaze; the compact pairing gives ضلال an eschatological end rather than an indefinite wandering.
luna: This verse asks whether people will be raised after death and becoming dust and bones, directly matching the section’s scene of bodies disappearing into earth.
luna: The question in 56:48 extends the dust objection to their forefathers, completing the scope of the denial in 56:47.
luna: This verse answers by saying earlier and later generations will be gathered at an appointed day; the hidden dead have a specified gathering rather than an unknown end.
luna: This verse names that gathering as the appointed meeting of the known Day; it completes the answer to the disappearance raised in 56:47–48.
terra: God knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, precisely the movement the source contrasts with a person thought to have vanished into ground.
luna: The section treats earth as the place where bodies disappear; this verse says God gives life to earth after its death, reversing the image of ground as a final hiding place.
luna: The section makes disappearance and what remains perceptible; this verse gives a specific image of worldly growth becoming yellow and debris, then contrasts it with the enduring Hereafter.
terra: God counts what people have forgotten and informs them of it; forgotten acts do not vanish from the record, as in 20:52.

luna: The verse says those who forget God are made to forget themselves; it develops the section’s connection between what disappears from memory and losing oneself. | terra: Forgetting God results in forgetting one's own selves, a moral version of the source's person who becomes lost beyond recognition.
luna: Disbelievers claim they will not be raised, and the answer affirms that they will be raised and informed of what they did; this directly opposes disappearance as an end.
terra: People are told to walk the earth's slopes, eat its provision, and remember that resurrection is to God; ordinary travel and final return share one directed horizon.
terra: Beside the command to walk the earth in 67:15, the warning that it may swallow people marks the boundary between a made-passable ground and sudden loss within it.

luna: The section’s road image distinguishes purposeful travel from losing one’s way; this verse contrasts someone moving face-down with someone walking upright on صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ. | terra: The face-down walker and the upright walker on a straight path embody two opposed ways of moving: disorientation versus guided progress.
terra: If water sinks deep into the earth, no one can recover it except through God; an essential resource becomes hidden below reach, echoing the source's water-and-ground losses.
terra: People emerge from graves and rush as if toward a marker, another image of buried persons moving visibly toward a summons.
terra: God causes humanity to grow from the earth like plants, preparing the return and re-emergence in the next ayah rather than treating earth as annihilation.
terra: God returns people to the earth and will bring them forth again, explicitly turning return-to-ground into a passage with an emergence.
terra: God spreads the earth for people, preparing the spatial setting for movement rather than an undifferentiated place of disappearance.

luna: The verse describes traveling through broad roads in the earth, concretely staging the movement along a way that the section uses to distinguish directed travel from aimless loss. | terra: Its purpose is that people travel its broad paths, an explicit traveler-and-way scene alongside the earth imagery.
terra: Those who submit seek the right way, distinguishing an actively sought course from the directionless state described by the source.
terra: Remaining straight on the way would bring abundant water; the verse ties a sustained route to provision in the very element where the source imagines disappearance.
terra: The human asks whether God will gather bones, directly challenging the idea that dispersed remains cannot be recovered.
terra: God is able even to proportion the fingertips, so the answer to the lost-body question is exact re-creation rather than a general promise.
terra: "There is no refuge" denies any place in which one can disappear from the coming encounter, a boundary akin to 82:16.
terra: On that Day the driving is to the Lord, giving final movement the destination that the source says ضَلال lacks.
terra: God shows the human the way, after which gratitude or ingratitude divides the response; the section's road is a disclosed route with a consequential choice.
terra: The earth is made a container, so its enclosing function gives a physical setting for the source's buried and hidden person.
terra: The next ayah specifies that the earth's enclosure includes both living and dead, joining the visible and buried conditions the source sets side by side.

luna: After people see what they sent ahead, the disbeliever wishes he were dust; this reverses the section’s question of whether becoming dust is final, since the dust wish comes after judgment is visible.
luna: The section says burial can look like disappearance without return; this verse voices the question whether people will be restored to their former state after death.
luna: This verse sharpens the objection by asking about return after becoming decayed bones, matching the section’s burial image.
luna: The objectors call resurrection كَرَّةٌ خَاسِرَةٌ, a losing return; this reverses the section’s distinction between aimless disappearance and a road that reaches its destination.
terra: Only one cry is needed for the resurrection, denying that hidden dead bodies are too dispersed to be summoned.
terra: After that cry, they are suddenly on the open surface, a sharp transition from concealment to visibility.
terra: After death God places the human in a grave; the act of being put out of sight is named as one stage of a divine sequence.
terra: After the grave of 80:21, God's will raises the person, making the concealed stage a pause before a known destination.
luna: The section’s dictionary wording describes someone who went away with no one knowing where; this verse asks فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ, directly making the destination of a departure the question.
luna: After the question about where people are going in 81:26, this verse says the reminder is for whoever wills to be upright; it contributes the alternative of choosing a directed course.
luna: This verse names the Day of Recompense and the fire they enter; the following verse, 82:16, says they cannot be absent from it, fixing the referent of the section’s no-disappearance claim.

luna: The section says no one can vanish from the Day of Recompense; this verse gives that boundary directly: وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ. | terra: وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ denies being absent from the Fire, the source's direct counterimage to vanishing from sight.
terra: The earth is spread out in the final upheaval, beginning the reversal of its normal capacity to hold what has disappeared into it.
terra: It casts out what is within it, a direct image of hidden contents no longer remaining lost in the earth.
terra: The earth obeys its Lord in releasing its contents, so the emergence in 84:4 is purposive rather than accidental.

luna: The section’s road traveler disappears from the observer yet has a destination; this verse describes each person striving toward his Lord and then meeting Him, giving travel an explicit endpoint. | terra: Every human labors onward toward the Lord and will meet Him, an exact thematic answer to the source's question whether a going has a destination.
terra: The Day when secrets are tested brings hidden things out for examination, a nonlexical parallel to the source's concern with what disappears from sight or memory.
luna: The section asks what direction a journey finally takes; this verse says people prefer the nearer life, naming the pull toward an immediate destination.
luna: This verse says the Hereafter is better and more lasting, giving a specific lasting destination against the nearer life preferred in 87:16.
luna: When Hell is brought near, a person remembers what he sent ahead; this reverses the section’s forgotten-event image by showing lost memory return at judgment.

luna: This verse says God showed the human two high paths; its image of distinct routes sharpens the section’s contrast between going along a path and losing one’s direction. | terra: The two ways are shown to the human, making direction a choice between courses rather than an unknowable disappearance.
luna: This verse says the person did not climb the steep pass; 90:12 begins to identify that pass, so this row contributes the refusal to take a difficult route with a moral destination.

luna: The section’s named root ض ل ل means being lost or out of sight, not simply the opposite of walking; this verse says God found the Prophet ضَالًّا and guided him, showing a lost state that can lead into guidance. | terra: "He found you ضَالًّا and guided" shares the source root and its reversal into guidance, but the precise sense of ضَالًّا here is interpretively broader than literal disappearance.

luna: The section describes the dead as lost when buried; this verse reverses that concealment when the earth throws out its burdens. | terra: The earth brings out its burdens; the source's lost-in-earth image meets a scene in which what it held becomes manifest.

luna: After the earth casts out its burdens in 99:2, it reports its news in this verse; what was hidden under it becomes testimony. | terra: The earth tells its news after bringing out its burdens, giving voice to the ground that had enclosed what was hidden.
terra: What is in graves is scattered out, turning a place of concealment into disclosure on the Day of reckoning.
terra: What lies in breasts is made manifest after the graves are opened, extending bodily emergence to the disclosure of concealed inner contents.
